pages.excerpt:
The**Ministry of Justice of Italy**([Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language):*Ministero della Giustizia*) is a department of the[government of Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics_of_Italy). Headquartered in[Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_(Italy)#cite_note-1)headed by the political official who serves as[Minister of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Minister_of_Justice).

## Background[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ministry_of_Justice_(Italy)&action=edit&section=1)]

In Italy, there is no strict equivalent of an[Attorney General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attorney_General), and all comparisons risk being misleading, due to the differences in the constitutional and legal systems. As a result, the very approximate equivalent of a U.S. Attorney General would be the**Ministro della Giustizia**, who is a member of the government and head of the Italian Department
